newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Living buys four facilities.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Living buys four facilities.

text.p: Integrated Living Communities Inc said Thursday it bought four Virginia-based assisted living facilities with a total of 198 beds for about $15 million in cash.
The company also said it signed letters of intent to buy eight other facilities with a total of 626 beds.
The acquisitions would give the company a total of 2,789 beds in 11 states, the company said.

The 198 beds would add about $4 million a year to the company's annual $36 million in revenues, while the 626 beds would add about $10 million a year, according to the company's chief financial officer, John Poole.

Poole said the company used most of a $16 million bridge loan to pay for the four Virginia facilities. The 626 beds would cost between $20 million and $25 million, he added. The company would pay for them through monthly leases and by transactions involving REITs, Poole said.
The company gets about $2,000 per month, per bed, he added.
Assisted living facilities are housing units that provide people with personal support and health care services, Poole said.
